name: Mouth widening appliance

card.summary: A mouth widening appliance is an intraoral stretching device that looksmaxxing forum members use in the hope of widening the mouth and smile corners for a broader, more balanced lower face.
card.note: Derived from clinical appliances for microstomia; no study has tested it for cosmetic widening.

quick.overview:
A mouth widening appliance is a rigid or semi-rigid device placed inside the mouth that presses outward on the corners of the lips. Users hope that repeated gentle stretching increases mouth width so the smile looks wider and the lower face better proportioned.

The idea borrows from medical devices used for microstomia, a condition of abnormally small mouth opening. Within looksmaxxing forums, people share 3D-printable designs in widths from 7 to 12 cm, DIY versions and commercial microstomia appliances, and post before-and-after pictures.
quick.how: Forum threads describe printing a model in a chosen width through a 3D printing service or buying a clinical appliance sold for microstomia prevention, then wearing it inside the mouth at intervals. Members discuss which width to choose and report results in threads. Timelines vary by account.
quick.risks: No published study has tested these appliances for widening a healthy mouth. In clinical use, microstomia appliances and exercises are directed by a healthcare professional. Forum members raise questions about downsides, such as smile lines and philtrum changes, in dedicated threads.

lead: A mouth widening appliance is a stretching device worn inside the mouth with the aim of widening the mouth and extending the corners of the smile. Looksmaxxing communities discuss mouth width as one proportion of the lower face and present the appliance as a non-surgical way to change it.[1][2]

The concept comes from clinical practice. Microstomia, an abnormally small mouth opening, can be congenital or follow burns or scleroderma, and clinicians manage it with surgery, prevention appliances, compression garments and therapist-guided exercise.[3] One forum thread asks whether a commercial 'adult microstomia prevention appliance' sold by a rehabilitation company is legitimate, and a reply describes it as 'pretty legit'.[4]

On looksmax.org, users share 3D models in sizes from 7 cm to 12 cm to be printed by a print shop, and the community has several guides, DIY designs and results threads.[2] No clinical studies have examined the devices for cosmetic widening.

angle.text: Users wear a stretching appliance in the hope of making the mouth wider so the smile reads broader and better matched to the face. The effect is claimed in forum threads and has not been measured in published studies.

infobox: 3D-printed (7-12 cm models), DIY, commercial clinical devices
No studies found for cosmetic use

paras: Appliances discussed in forums are rigid bars or frames sized to the target mouth width, placed between the corners of the lips.[2] Threads include DIY tool ideas and discussions of an alternative design intended to avoid smile lines.[5][6]

Models are shared as files for printing; one thread notes that someone without a printer can order the print from a service shop and that no account is needed beyond a free design site to export the file.[2]

Microstomia is treated clinically with intraoral appliances, manual stretching or exercises guided by speech or occupational therapists, and surgery to release scar tension. The literature stresses early, consistent intervention directed by a qualified clinician.[3]

Members discuss mouth width as part of facial harmony and debate whether widening could help issues such as a long philtrum.[7] Other threads cover ordering appliances, 'results' posts and questions about downsides.[8][9]
No studies found. Published literature on appliances concerns microstomia in patients, not cosmetic widening of a healthy mouth.[3]

lore.intro: Mouth widening is a recurring topic on looksmax.org, with guides, results threads and questions about whether the effect is real.[2][4]

claims.claim: Wearing a widening appliance can permanently widen the mouth
claims.believers: Users post before-and-after pictures and say the change makes most people look better.[10]
claims.experts: No published study has tested stretching appliances for cosmetic widening; clinical literature concerns microstomia.[3]

claims.claim: Clinical microstomia appliances are the legitimate version of the approach
claims.believers: A forum reply calls a commercial microstomia appliance 'pretty legit'.[4]
claims.experts: Clinicians use such devices for patients with scarring or syndromes, under professional direction.[3]
